clue.text: Exchange the stage for call-girls' work

parts.note: to exchange one thing for another is to switch them
the boards is a theatrical name for the stage, as in 'treading the boards'

explanation.surface: Someone trades a theatre career for prostitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call-girls' here are not prostitutes but the women who once connected telephone calls by hand at a switchboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephone operators, once nicknamed call girls, worked at manual exchange panels connecting callers.

clue.text: Divide up undercover agents into group

indicators.note: the agents go into the group

parts.note: a set is a group of things
G-men is slang for FBI agents

explanation.surface: Secret agents are split up and assigned to a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To break something into parts or sections is to divide it.

clue.text: Finger book-list

definitions.meaning: the forefinger is called the ... finger
an alphabetical list of topics at the back of a book

explanation.surface: Someone points at a list of books.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointing digit next to the thumb bears this name, as does the alphabetical subject list in a book.

clue.text: Daughter gone, decline and fall of Wordsworth's inspiration

indicators.note: the letters fall into a new order
the daughter is gone, so her letter is removed

explanation.surface: A father's decline and fall after his daughter leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes one D from DECLINE AND, and 'fall' rearranges the remaining nine letters. Wordsworth wrote three poems to the small celandine.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow spring flower was the subject of several of the poet's verses.

clue.text: Inlaid work up the nave at end of wall

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the nave of a wheel is its hub

indicators.note: only the end of wall, its last letter, is used

explanation.surface: Decoration climbs the church nave to the end of a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nave' suggests a church, but it is the hub of a wheel. Buhl is brass and tortoiseshell marquetry, also spelt boulle.
explanation.definitionFit: Boulle marquetry is decorative inlay of brass and tortoiseshell on furniture.

clue.text: Having no faith in a mystic

parts.note: a Gnostic claims mystical knowledge of the divine

explanation.surface: Someone lacks belief in a mystic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: One who holds that God's existence cannot be known lacks religious belief.

clue.text: Bertie's clubmate cheated about run

indicators.note: the word for cheated goes about the letter for run

parts.note: to be done is to be cheated or swindled
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A fellow club member of Bertie cheated over a run.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster, of P G Wodehouse's stories, belongs to the Drones Club, whose members are drones.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Wodehouse's idle young men's club are called after the lazy male bees.

clue.text: Leather, starting to crack, spoiled door on wagon

indicators.note: starting to crack gives only the first letter of crack
spoiled letters are damaged and rearranged

parts.note: a van is a covered wagon or goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A leather-covered wagon door starts to crack and is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' turns DOOR into ORDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordovan is a fine leather originally from Cordoba in Spain.

clue.text: Tree is dead or mutilated

indicators.note: mutilated words are cut about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree is either dead or badly damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan cedar is a large evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Stuart Lord Treasurer from whom some Arabs took their line

definitions.text: from whom some Arabs took their line

explanation.surface: A royal minister is credited as ancestor of a line of Arabs.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidney Godolphin was Lord Treasurer under Queen Anne, the last Stuart monarch; the Godolphin Arabian, a stallion named after his family, is a founding sire of the Thoroughbred racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: The earl served Queen Anne as chief finance minister, and the famous foundation stallion of racing bloodlines bore the family title.

clue.text: Ought girdle to form protective layer?

parts.note: ought (nought) is zero, written as the letter O
a zone is an old word for a belt or girdle

explanation.surface: Should a girdle be worn as a protective layer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ought' looks like the verb 'should' but is the old word for nought, zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratospheric gas forms a shield absorbing ultraviolet radiation from the sun.

clue.text: Main title the friendly Greeks conferred

definitions.text: Main title the friendly Greeks conferred

parts.words: Main title the friendly Greeks conferred
parts.note: 'main' is the sea, and the Greeks called the stormy Black Sea by a name meaning 'hospitable', hoping to placate it

explanation.surface: An honour bestowed by amiable Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as 'chief', but in crosswords it is the sea; the Greek name Pontos Euxeinos means 'hospitable sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient classical name for the Black Sea came from a Greek word meaning welcoming to strangers.

clue.text: Add scene in new version for Rose

indicators.note: putting the words into a new version rewrites their letters in a different order

explanation.surface: A director inserts an extra scene in a new version of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a flower or a name, but it is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are past tenses meaning went up or climbed.

clue.text: Delicacy a bird snapped at

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
to snap at with the teeth is to bite, past tense bit

explanation.surface: A tasty morsel that some bird pecked at.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice morsel of food is a tasty treat or delicacy.

clue.text: Not, they say, a chance of decisive court action

parts.note: 'not' said aloud is 'knot', and a knot is a tie
a break is a chance or opportunity, as in a lucky break

explanation.surface: People claim there is no chance of decisive legal proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court, but this is a tennis court. 'Not, they say' looks like denial but is a homophone of knot.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a deciding game played when a set reaches six games all settles the set.

clue.text: Find that the recording has finished

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record, a recording
something that has finished is over

explanation.surface: Someone learns that the record has come to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon or learn something new is to find it.

clue.text: Devonshire name for tobacco

definitions.meaning: the family name of the Dukes of Devonshire
a sweetened, pressed tobacco for pipes

explanation.surface: A Devon name given to a brand of tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devonshire' suggests the English county, but it is the dukedom, held by the Cavendish family.
explanation.definitionFit: The dukes' surname is shared by a pressed, sweetened pipe tobacco cake.

clue.text: It's not what the soldier said in Pickwick's trial

definitions.text: It's not what the soldier said in Pickwick's trial

parts.words: It's not what the soldier said in Pickwick's trial
parts.note: in Dickens's Pickwick Papers, the judge at the breach-of-promise trial stops Sam Weller quoting a soldier, ruling hearsay inadmissible

explanation.surface: A recollection of the courtroom scene in Pickwick Papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Weller tells the court what a soldier said, and the judge replies, 'You must not tell us what the soldier said... it's not ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is not admissible proof in court, which is what the judge told Sam Weller.

clue.text: Keep quiet about free verse

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet
re is Latin for about, concerning

indicators.note: free verse has no fixed form, so the letters of verse are set free to rearrange

explanation.surface: Advice to say nothing about unrhymed poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' makes SERVE from the letters of 'verse'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something is to save or maintain it unchanged.

clue.text: Fluorine doubled in reactor? Rubbish!

indicators.note: the doubled letter goes in the word for reactor

parts.note: an atomic pile is an early name for a nuclear reactor

indicators.note: the fluorine symbol is doubled, written twice

parts.note: F is the chemical symbol for fluorine

explanation.surface: A chemist scoffs at the idea of doubling the fluorine in a reactor.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffle is nonsense, an exclamation of contempt.

clue.text: Steven has lost way to London square

indicators.note: Steven has lost some letters, so they are taken out of his name

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
travelling to London from anywhere in Britain is traditionally going up

explanation.surface: A man named Steven gets lost on his way to a London square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost' removes ST from STEVEN to leave EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To level things out or settle a balance is to square them.

clue.text: Severely criticize each new display

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it severely

indicators.note: new letters are a fresh arrangement of the word each

explanation.surface: A critic savages every new exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns EACH into ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant confidence of style is a showy display.

clue.text: Dispatches pack for key sections

parts.note: taken as written
the wards are the notches and ridges of a key that match a lock

explanation.surface: Military dispatches bundled up for important units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack' is a second definition: the forwards are a rugby team's pack. 'key sections' looks like 'important parts' but means the cut parts of an actual key.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch a letter onward is to send it on, a usage seen in mail redirection.

clue.text: The silver copy is for charity

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
to ape someone is to copy or mimic them

explanation.surface: A silver replica is donated to charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charity' is the old sense of Christian love, as in 1 Corinthians 13; agape is the Greek word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for selfless Christian love was translated as charity in the King James Bible.

clue.text: Scots ban. I hear, casts a shadow on Sundays

indicators.note: the setter says what he hears, so the words are taken for their sound

parts.note: a Scot forbidding something might say 'No, mon!', Scots for 'no, man'

explanation.surface: A Scottish prohibition seems to spoil the Sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sundays' is to be read as 'sun days': the pointer on a sundial throws its shadow only when the sun shines. The silent G makes the sound fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright pointer of a sundial is the part whose shadow tells the time.

clue.text: I would overplay rise of Sudanese rebel

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letters rise from the bottom, read backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
to ham is to overplay a role

explanation.surface: An actor admits overacting the rise of a Sudanese rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns IDHAM into MAHDI. The Mahdi led the 1880s revolt in Sudan against Egyptian rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ahmad, the self-styled messiah, led the uprising that killed General Gordon at Khartoum.

clue.text: Helmer's wife is no academician

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Helmer's wife is no academic.
explanation.walkthrough: Torvald Helmer's wife is the heroine of Ibsen's A Doll's House.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's heroine who walks out on her husband in A Doll's House is Mrs Helmer.

clue.text: Start to haunt a quarter in the French capital

indicators.note: these letters sit in the French article

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

indicators.note: only the start of the word haunt is wanted, its first letter

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A ghost begins to haunt a district of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' seems to mean Paris but is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetan city is the seat of that region's government.

clue.text: Sort of hot line Channel islands rejected — very primitive type

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters are sorted anew
rejected things are sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off Normandy

explanation.surface: A telephone hotline to the Channel Islands is refused, being hopelessly old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' turns HOTLINE into NEOLITH; 'rejected' turns CI into IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Late Stone Age people are the archetype of the primitive.

clue.text: Paris underground station — last stop for some

explanation.surface: A Metro stop described as the end of the line for some travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Père Lachaise metro station serves the famous Paris cemetery, a final resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: The station on the Paris Metro shares its name with the great cemetery where many are buried, their final destination.
